page: Amazon Web Services c5.metal is a bare-metal instance within the compute-optimized family, providing direct hardware access without hypervisor virtualization. It is powered by dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8275CL processors running at 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB per core compute-optimized ratio. Cache allocation includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and cryptographic AES acceleration. The system features no bundled local storage and no GPUs, relying on remote network storage interfaces supported by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput across highly parallel and compute-intensive operations. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a stress-ng multi-core score of 95,252.05 and a PassMark CPU score of 63,325.12, placing in the top 25%. It performs strongly in tasks such as Clang code compilation (49,722.0) and ray tracing (58,945.0). Memory throughput is elevated, delivering 235.82 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 97.79 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, paired with a PassMark memory score of 2,922.77. Operational throughput tests confirm solid performance for in-memory systems and high-concurrency routing, yielding 82.96 million Redis SET operations per second and 47.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

In contrast, single-threaded processing and generative AI tasks demonstrate noticeable tradeoffs. Single-core evaluations, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,456.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,627.0, fall within the middle 50% range. While LLM prompt processing is moderate (2,180.76 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 129.16 tokens/sec on a 7B model), token generation speeds fall into the bottom 10% (40.56 tokens/sec on 135M and 5.21 tokens/sec on 7B) due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, c5.metal provides dense multi-threaded CPU compute and direct bare-metal hardware control, making it efficient for workloads requiring non-virtualized access, custom virtualization stacks, or sustained parallel processing. Because the instance lacks local storage, operational storage costs depend entirely on network-attached volumes. The hardware configuration makes this server best suited for large-scale CI/CD build environments, batch compute processing, distributed compiling, and high-concurrency database or caching operations.

The instance includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory (2.0 GB per core) and baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with no local storage or GPUs bundled. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 95,252.05, strong Clang software compilation throughput, and 82.96 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain moderate, and LLM text generation rates fall into the lower tiers due to CPU-bound execution. With direct bare-metal access and dense parallelism, c5.metal is structured for distributed CI/CD builds, intensive batch compute, and high-throughput caching systems.
